analyst.summary: Mazagon Dock is India's leading warship and submarine PSU shipyard, debt-free and consistently profitable, but its own order book has shrunk 59% from its FY21 peak (Rs 49,700cr) to Rs 20,535cr as of March 2026 as the P-17A frigate program it was building has now been fully delivered -- leaving only about two years of confirmed revenue visibility. The stock's ~38-42x earnings multiple is betting on a large pending pipeline (the Rs 70,000-99,000 crore Project-75I submarine deal, a further Scorpene-class order) converting into signed contracts roughly on schedule; as of this research neither has been signed -- P-75I has cleared Finance Ministry approval but still awaits final government sign-off, months past management's own original target date, and Mazagon Dock has already lost one live defence tender (the Next-Generation Corvette) to a rival PSU shipyard. FY26 profit growth (6.8% for the year) was also partly helped by lower provisioning and a large slice of profit coming from interest income rather than core shipbuilding margin, which are not the same as sustainable operating improvement. Given the gap between a full core order book that is depleting and a valuation that already assumes the next mega-orders land on time, the risk-reward looks unfavourable at current levels.
